intro: Who's actually building mitochondrial medicine, a hand-kept watchlist of 40+ biotech and pharma companies. Filter by stage, mechanism, or indication. Details change fast; treat this as a starting point and verify on each company's own site.
disclaimer: Compiled from public information and my own reading. Stages, mechanisms and indications shift constantly, always confirm on the company's site and ClinicalTrials.gov. This is not investment advice.

companies.name: x-tosis
companies.coi: Full disclosure: I co-founded this one. It's on the list because it belongs on any VDAC1 watchlist, not as a recommendation. Grain of salt fully provided.
companies.blurb: First-in-class VDAC1-modulating mitochondrial therapeutics for neurodegeneration, aiming upstream, at the biology of neuronal death itself, rather than downstream symptoms. "Saving brain cells." Based in Gainesville, Florida.

companies.name: Stealth BioTherapeutics
companies.blurb: The most clinically advanced name in the field. Peptide elamipretide (SS-31) targets cardiolipin on the inner mitochondrial membrane to shore up energy, furthest along in dry AMD and primary mitochondrial myopathy.

companies.name: Abliva
companies.blurb: Swedish, spun out of NeuroVive. Lead drug KL1333 is an NAD+ modulator meant to restore cellular energy in genetically defined mitochondrial disease (the FALCON program in MELAS-type patients).

companies.name: Khondrion
companies.blurb: Dutch clinical-stage biotech founded by a mitochondrial-medicine physician. Sonlicromanol (KH176) is an oral redox modulator tested in mitochondrial disease (MELAS) and now post-COVID.

companies.name: PTC Therapeutics
companies.blurb: A larger rare-disease company with a real mitochondrial footprint, vatiquinone targets oxidative stress (15-lipoxygenase) in Friedreich's ataxia and inherited mitochondrial disease.

companies.name: Mission Therapeutics
companies.blurb: The one I watch most for VDAC-adjacent reasons: they inhibit the deubiquitinase USP30 to unleash mitophagy, clearing damaged mitochondria, with programs in kidney disease and Parkinson's.

companies.name: Larimar Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Protein-replacement play: nomlabofusp delivers frataxin, the protein missing in Friedreich's ataxia, into mitochondria to restore iron–sulfur cluster biology.

companies.name: Minovia Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Israeli pioneer of mitochondrial augmentation therapy (MAT), enriching a patient's own stem cells with healthy mitochondria, in Pearson syndrome and other primary mitochondrial diseases.

companies.name: cellvie
companies.blurb: Betting on mitochondrial transplantation, delivering isolated, functional mitochondria as a therapeutic, starting with ischemia–reperfusion injury and transplant medicine.

companies.name: Luca Science
companies.blurb: Japanese biotech developing stabilized functional mitochondria and mitochondria-derived therapeutics for acute organ injury and energy-starved tissues.

companies.name: Astellas (ex-Mitobridge)
companies.blurb: Big pharma in the space via its 2017 acquisition of Mitobridge, PPARδ agonism to drive mitochondrial biogenesis, explored in primary mitochondrial myopathy and acute kidney injury.

companies.name: Pretzel Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Well-funded newcomer going after mitochondrial DNA replication and quality control, tuning how cells make and maintain their mitochondrial genome. One to watch.

companies.name: MitoRx Therapeutics
companies.blurb: UK biotech designing small molecules that protect mitochondria from oxidative damage, with programs pointed at Parkinson's, Friedreich's ataxia and muscular dystrophy.

companies.name: Mitochon Pharmaceuticals
companies.blurb: Developing controlled mitochondrial uncouplers (MP101/MP201), gently 'leaking' the membrane to cut oxidative stress, for ALS, MS and traumatic brain injury.

companies.name: Biogen (Skyclarys)
companies.blurb: Omaveloxolone (Skyclarys), an Nrf2 activator that reboots antioxidant and mitochondrial gene programs, is the first FDA-approved drug for Friedreich's ataxia (via the Reata acquisition).

companies.name: Reneo / OnKure
companies.blurb: Mavodelpar (REN001) is a PPARδ agonist meant to boost mitochondrial biogenesis and fatty-acid oxidation in primary mitochondrial myopathies.

companies.name: Design Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Gene-targeted chimeras (GeneTACs) aimed at the repeat expansion that silences frataxin, trying to fix Friedreich's ataxia at the DNA level.

companies.name: Lexeo Therapeutics
companies.blurb: AAV gene therapy delivering frataxin to the heart, targeting the cardiomyopathy that's the leading cause of death in Friedreich's ataxia.

companies.name: Taysha Gene Therapies
companies.blurb: AAV gene therapies for severe monogenic CNS disease, including Rett syndrome and other conditions where mitochondrial and metabolic failure drive neuronal loss.

companies.name: Anavex Life Sciences
companies.blurb: Blarcamesine activates the sigma-1 receptor at the ER–mitochondria interface (the MAM), aiming to restore cellular homeostasis in Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and Rett syndrome.

companies.name: Clene
companies.blurb: CNM-Au8 is a suspension of gold nanocrystals that catalytically supports the NAD+/NADH balance to keep neurons energized, in late-stage trials for ALS and multiple sclerosis.

companies.name: Biojiva (ex-Retrotope)
companies.blurb: Deuterium-stabilized fatty acids that resist lipid peroxidation, protecting mitochondrial membranes, in Friedreich's ataxia, ALS and infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy.

companies.name: Denali Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Broad neurodegeneration player whose programs touch mitochondrial and lysosomal quality control (e.g. LRRK2) in Parkinson's and ALS.

companies.name: Epirium Bio
companies.blurb: Small molecules that stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis to rebuild muscle and nerve energy capacity, aimed at neuromuscular disease.

companies.name: Solid Biosciences
companies.blurb: Best known for Duchenne gene therapy, now expanding into gene therapies for inherited cardiac conditions, including mitochondrial cardiomyopathies.

companies.name: Amazentis (Timeline / Mitopure)
companies.blurb: Swiss biotech (EPFL spinout) that discovered and holds the IP on urolithin A, a gut-metabolite that induces mitophagy; ran the human clinical trials (published in Nature Metabolism and JAMA Network Open) establishing its muscle and mitochondrial effects before licensing it as Mitopure.

companies.name: Metro International Biotech
companies.blurb: David Sinclair-founded, developing next-gen NAD+ boosters (MIB-626) as actual drugs, in clinical testing for metabolic and age-related decline.

companies.name: Life Biosciences
companies.blurb: Partial epigenetic reprogramming to restore youthful cell function, with mitochondrial and metabolic rejuvenation central to the thesis; lead program in optic neuropathy.

companies.name: BioAge Labs
companies.blurb: Mines human ageing data for targets in muscle and metabolic decline, where mitochondrial function is a recurring theme, and runs clinical metabolic programs.

companies.name: Cambrian Bio
companies.blurb: A 'rejuvenation' holding company with a pipeline of ageing-biology programs, several centered on mitochondrial and metabolic health.

companies.name: Gordian Biotechnology
companies.blurb: Runs in-vivo pooled screens (many perturbations in one animal) to find drivers of age-related decline, mitochondrial dysfunction squarely in scope.

companies.name: Continuum Biosciences
companies.blurb: Developing 'mitochondrial enhancers', mild uncoupling and redox tuning, to raise baseline mitochondrial resilience in ageing and neurodegeneration.

companies.name: NRG Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Early-stage UK biotech developing small-molecule inhibitors of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore, the structure whose prolonged opening drives neuronal death in ALS and Parkinson's.

companies.name: Mitokinin
companies.blurb: Early-stage biotech developing small-molecule activators of PINK1, the kinase that kicks off mitophagy, as a disease-modifying approach to Parkinson's rather than a symptom treatment.

companies.name: Vandria
companies.blurb: Swiss biotech spun out of EPFL, developing small molecules that activate mitophagy directly, targeting neurodegeneration and other diseases where clearing damaged mitochondria could help.

companies.name: Casma Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Biotech built around activating autophagy, including mitophagy, with small molecules; a broader cellular-quality-control platform with programs touching neurodegeneration.

companies.name: BPGbio
companies.blurb: Uses an AI-driven mitochondrial-biology platform to find drugs that target cancer metabolism; lead candidate BPM31510 (a CoQ10-based therapy) has been tested in glioblastoma and pancreatic cancer.

companies.name: Sinopia Biosciences
companies.blurb: Clinical-stage biotech developing an optimized formulation of dichloroacetate, a pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase inhibitor, for Leigh syndrome and other primary mitochondrial diseases.

companies.name: CoA Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Early-stage biotech working to restore coenzyme A levels for PKAN, a genetic disorder that causes mitochondrial iron accumulation and neurodegeneration.

companies.name: NeuroSense Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Clinical-stage biotech developing PrimeC, a combination therapy for ALS that includes an iron-chelation component thought to help protect motor-neuron mitochondrial function.

companies.name: Rocket Pharmaceuticals
companies.blurb: Gene-therapy company with a late-stage program for Danon disease, caused by defective autophagy (including mitophagy) that leads to severe cardiomyopathy.

companies.name: Pheno Therapeutics
companies.blurb: Early-stage UK biotech targeting cellular senescence, a state in which dysfunctional mitochondria are a defining hallmark, aiming to ease age-related tissue decline.

companies.name: Rejuveron Life Sciences
companies.blurb: Swiss longevity biotech with multiple subsidiaries working on senescence, the gut-brain axis and other aging biology, several with mitochondrial-health angles.

companies.name: Retro Biosciences
companies.blurb: Longevity biotech working on partial cellular reprogramming, plasma-based therapeutics and autophagy induction, with mitochondrial rejuvenation as part of the underlying biology.
